notes:
Lead: CTO (Marina Gould) very focused on deterministic latency for live-bridge chat. Wants p99 < 400ms for short-turn queries and p95 < 200ms for user-facing assistant.
Workload details: mix of chat and reranking. Chat avg tokens/request: 60-110 (median 78). Reranking requests small (10-20 tokens) but high QPS bursts.
Traffic patterns: steady-state 35-50 QPS day, spikes to 180 QPS during fleet check-ins (5-10 minute bursts every 4 hours).

workshop_summary:
Goal: translate traffic trace into reserved GPU plan and SLA request. SE walked through tokenized traces, per-model tokens/sec estimates, and estimated effective QPS per GPU given concurrency and batching. Identified two dominant shapes: chat (variable tokens, latency-sensitive) and rerank (tiny tokens, CPU-friendly but throughput-bound). Discussed hybrid routing: warm dedicated pool for chat + burst pool for rerank.
Outcome: agreed to run second workshop with 24h of tokenized production trace and confirm p99 latency test vectors. Also agreed to propose two capacity options (Conservative = 6 reserved GPUs; Aggressive = 3 reserved GPUs + autoscale burst).
sizing_recommendation:
Initial recommendation (ballpark):
- Baseline steady-state: reserve 3 x A100-80GB equiv for chat workload (assume 400 tokens/sec per GPU for quantized 13B with batching + KV cache) to handle ~3,600 tokens/sec steady (45 QPS * 80 tokens).
- Peak headroom: additional 2 x A100-80GB equiv as reserved burst capacity to cover 180 QPS 10-min bursts (target 25-30% utilisation headroom).
- Reranking: colocate small CPU/FP16 instances or small GPU pool (1 x T4-equivalent) for high-QPS small-token rerank jobs and use batching.
- Routing: primary route to dedicated chat pool with strict concurrency limits; fallback to quantized 7B (lower latency but lower quality) when queue depth exceeds threshold.
Notes: numbers subject to change after ingesting 24h tokenized trace and running microbenchmarks in Redwood test harness.
sla_expectations:
Requested SLA: 99.9% uptime, p99 latency < 400ms for chat (context <= 2k tokens), p95 < 200ms for interactive turns. Redwood should propose SLA credits and response playbook for fallback scenarios. Legal asked for clarity on force majeure and maintenance windows.
Proposed Redwood position: SLA with rolling credits, 4-hour incident response for P2, testing window before SLA becomes binding. Procurement has flagged liability cap as a blocker.
